heroSummary: For 2026–27, K–12 students in Denver Public Schools start school Monday, August 24. Early Childhood Education students start Tuesday, August 25. The last day of school is Friday, June 4, with a half-day early release. Thanksgiving Break runs November 23–27, Winter Break runs December 21–January 1, and Spring Break runs March 29–April 2. These are districtwide dates from the DPS family and student calendar. Individual schools may publish additional dates for testing, conferences, athletics, transportation changes, bell schedules, and other school events.
calendarNotes: DPS uses several calendar labels that matter for family planning: holidays/no classes, conference/no classes, vacation/no classes, planning and professional learning days, and other holidays and observances when school is open. The PDF also notes that some Jewish and Islamic holy days are based on moon sightings and may vary by a day.

sourceReviewSummary: This page is based on the DPS calendars page and the official 2026–27 English family and student calendar PDF.
sourceReviewDetails: August 4, 2026 — All districtwide dates on this page were checked against the DPS calendar page and the English PDF created June 17, 2026.

We checked the K–12 first day, ECE first day, last day, student contact-day count, teacher contact-day count, holidays/no classes, vacation/no-class dates, conference/no-class dates, planning/professional learning dates, and post-school-year district holidays shown in the PDF.
The DPS PDF lists 174.5 student contact days and 186 teacher contact days.
DPS states that other holidays and observances are marked separately and that school is open on those observance dates unless a date is also marked as no classes.

calendarFaqs.q: Do ECE students start on the same day as K–12 students?
calendarFaqs.a: No. K–12 students start Monday, August 24, 2026. Early Childhood Education students start Tuesday, August 25.

calendarFaqs.q: Is January 4 part of Winter Break?
calendarFaqs.a: Winter Break ends Friday, January 1, 2027. Monday, January 4 is a planning and professional learning day, so students return Tuesday, January 5.

calendarFaqs.q: Does every DPS holiday or observance mean school is closed?
calendarFaqs.a: No. On the official DPS calendar, some dates are marked as holidays or observances even when school remains open. Look for a separate no-classes designation before assuming students are off.

calendarFaqs.q: Does the downloaded DPS calendar update automatically?
calendarFaqs.a: The .ics file is a one-time import, not a live calendar subscription. Download a new copy if DPS publishes a revised calendar.

calendarFaqs.q: Does this calendar include school-specific events?
calendarFaqs.a: This page covers districtwide dates only. Individual schools may publish separate dates for testing, conferences, athletics, transportation changes, bell schedules, and same-day announcements.

customSections.content: The DPS calendar uses different markings for holidays, vacation periods, planning and professional learning days, conferences, and observances. These distinctions matter because not every holiday or observance is a day off for students.
